text:
The Indian market posted a strong week, with the Nifty 50 closing at 25,030.35, up 8.58%, and Bank Nifty at 59,086, up 8.04%. Broad market health was “HEALTHY” (breadth score 67.3), with 71.2% of stocks above their 20‑day average. Foreign Institutional Investors kept buying – net INR 45,960 crore for eight sessions – while Domestic Institutional Investors sold net INR 24,197 crore for six sessions. Volatility rose, the India VIX at 17.47 (+14.15%).  

Recent IPO activity was limited to listings that completed this week. Bombay Coated and Special Steels debuted on 5 Nov at an issue price of ₹82, opening 11% higher and closing 9.8% above issue. BLS Polymers listed on 3 Nov at ₹150, jumping 65.3% on the first day and ending 57.2% up. SFC Environmental Technologies opened at ₹330, up 7.6% and later 25.2% higher. Other listings – M.K. Sons Fine Jewels, EAAA India Alternatives, Paras Healthcare, Jio Platforms and Bonfiglioli – all closed above their issue prices, ranging from modest gains to a 25.7% rise for Jio. No new IPOs are scheduled for the coming week.  

Looking ahead, external factors could sway sentiment. Crude oil fell 16.98% to $97.66, easing inflation pressure, while gold rose 4.07% to $4,057.5, supporting a risk‑off tilt. The US equity futures slipped (S&P 500 ‑2.26%, Nasdaq ‑4.36%) and US mid‑term elections may trigger sector rotation, with healthcare highlighted as a potential beneficiary. Domestically, the USD‑INR eased 1.32% to 93.89, and the Hang Seng gained 5.10%, indicating mixed global cues that may influence the next week’s market direction.
